title: Preservation theorems: substructures and extensions
summary: Characterize universal axioms by closure under substructures, and existential formulas by preservation under extensions.
abstract: Suppose a first-order property remains true whenever a structure is enlarged. Does that tell us how the property can be written? An existential formula keeps its witnesses in an extension, and the preservation theorem gives a converse: every formula preserved under extensions is equivalent to an existential formula. The equivalence can also be restricted to models of a background theory. In the other direction, a first-order theory can be axiomatized by universal sentences exactly when its models are closed under nonempty substructures. These results turn facts about the relationships between models into descriptions of their properties by particular quantifier forms.
